q: The Election Commission of India is established under:
explanation: Art 324: superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, state legislatures, President and VP. 315 = PSCs; 280 = FC; 148 = CAG — the article-anchor drill.

q: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed:
options: Only in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge
explanation: Art 324(5): the CEC is removable only like an SC judge (special-majority address on proved misbehaviour/incapacity); other Election Commissioners are removable on the CEC's recommendation — the deliberate asymmetry.

q: Under the 2023 CEC Appointment Act, the selection committee comprises:
options: PM + Leader of Opposition (LS) + a Union Cabinet Minister
explanation: The 2023 Act: PM + LoP + Union Cabinet Minister — the CJI was dropped from Anoop Baranwal's interim formula (2023) — the newest exam point in this topic.

q: The Bihar Public Service Commission's members are appointed by:
explanation: Art 316: the Governor appoints SPSC members (for nearly half the posts, consultation with the UPSC is the convention under Art 316(2)); but only the President can remove them — BPSC's own constitutional basis.

q: A State PSC member can be removed from office by:
explanation: The appointment-removal asymmetry: the Governor appoints but only the President can remove (Art 317) — the constitutional insulation of SPSC members.

q: The advice of the UPSC/SPSC to the government is:
options: Not binding — but the government must return reasons for rejection (Art 320(3))
explanation: PSC advice is not binding; the government must communicate reasons for non-acceptance. Also: PSCs are NOT consulted on reservation policies — the two standard traps.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by:
options: The President; removable like an SC judge
explanation: Art 148: the President appoints the CAG; removal = SC-judge grade (special-majority address); salary charged on the CF; ineligible for further government office.

q: The CAG submits audit reports to:
options: The President (Union reports) / Governor (state reports), who lay them before Parliament/legislature
explanation: Art 151: reports go to the President/Governor → laid before Parliament/legislature → the PAC examines them (Topic 43's chain). The CAG never reports to Parliament directly.

q: The Finance Commission consists of:
options: Five members total including the chair
A chairperson and four other members
explanation: Art 280: chair + 4 members (5 total) appointed by the President every 5th year; 16th FC chair: Arvind Panagariya (2024-).

q: [71st BPSC] The Attorney General of India has the right to:
options: Sit only in the Rajya Sabha
Speak and participate in Parliament (and committees) without a vote; audience in all courts
explanation: Art 88/76: the AG speaks/participates in both Houses + committees without voting; audience in all courts — 71st BPSC's exact answer. Holds office at the President's pleasure.

q: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes was created by:
options: The 89th Amendment (2003), splitting the combined commission
explanation: 89th Amdt (2003): Art 338 (NCSC) + Art 338A (NCST) — the bifurcation of the earlier combined commission. The 102nd (2018) constitutionalised the NCBC (Art 338B).

q: The National Human Rights Commission is:
options: A statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act 1993
explanation: NHRC = statutory (PHRA 1993) — the classic classification trap. Chair: a retired CJI; 2023 amendment expanded composition.

q: The first Comptroller and Auditor General of independent India was:
explanation: V. Narahari Rao (1950) — the first CAG of independent India; the office traces to the 1858 Auditor-General (colonial predecessor); current duties under the CAG (DPC) Act 1971.

q: The expenses of the Election Commission are charged on:
explanation: EC/UPSC/SPSC/CAG/FC expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund — non-votable (Art 322 for PSCs; CAG's salary under 148(6)) — the independence-insulation trio.

q: The Advocate General of a state (Art 165):
options: Is appointed by the Governor; advises the state government; participates in the legislature without voting
Has voting rights in the council
explanation: Art 165: the Governor appoints the Advocate General (qualified as an HC judge); the state's chief legal adviser; assembly-audience without vote — the state mirror of the Union AG.

q: The UPSC is NOT consulted on:
options: Reservation policy and cadre rules' reservation aspects
explanation: UPSC advice excludes reservations (policy) — recruitment/promotion/discipline are consulted matters; the reservation-exclusion is the standard trap.

q: Which is NOT a constitutional body?
explanation: NHRC = statutory (1993 Act); FC (280), NCSC (338), EC (324) are constitutional — the classification drill's cleanest form.

q: The Anoop Baranwal case (2023) concerned:
options: Election Commissioners' appointments — SC prescribed PM + LoP + CJI until Parliament legislates
explanation: Anoop Baranwal (March 2023): SC's interim committee (PM + LoP + CJI) for EC appointments; Parliament's 2023 Act then replaced the CJI with a Cabinet Minister — the appointment saga's sequence.

q: The National Commission for Backward Classes got constitutional status through:
explanation: 102nd Amdt (2018): Art 338B — NCBC constitutionalised; also inserted 342A (state OBC lists — the Maratha litigation context).
EC = 324; CAG = 148-151; UPSC = 315-323; FC = 280 — the master anchor set every BPSC paper samples from.

q: The CAG is NOT eligible for further office under:
options: The Government of India or any state (post-retirement)
explanation: Art 148(4): the CAG is ineligible for further office under GoI or a state after ceasing to hold office — the insulation clause (mirrors UPSC members' bar under Art 319).

q: The Finance Commission's recommendations cover:
options: Tax devolution between the Union and states; grants-in-aid; augmenting local-body funds
explanation: Art 280(3): vertical/horizontal devolution, grants-in-aid (275), local-body grants (280(3)(bb) — panchayat/municipality funds), plus supplementary measures — Bihar's ~10% share flows from this machinery.

q: Bihar's share of the divisible pool (15th FC) makes it:
options: The largest recipient state share among all states
explanation: Bihar's ~10.06% is the highest single-state share after UP's ~18% — driven by the income-distance criterion (poorest states gain most) — the 'top recipient' framing is the exam-safe version.

q: The EC's Model Code of Conduct is:
options: A statutory code under the RP Act 1951
A set of conventions evolved (1960s-79) with the EC's enforcement power — not statute
explanation: MCC = conventions (first used in Kerala 1960; nationally adopted from 1979) enforced via Art 324's plenary powers — not statute; violations invite EC action (campaign freezes etc.).

q: Which body audits all bodies substantially financed by the Consolidated Fund?
explanation: Art 149-150: the CAG audits the Union, states, and any body/authority substantially financed from the CF — the audit universe; the PAC merely examines the CAG's reports.
